rationale: Submitted the recovery-authority probe for the ballot question: two ordinary owner-side recovery attempts blocked by the peers' higher stored ballot, then the same attempt after the target's own BeTheLeader authority, with the target's own messages and handler state as observations.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) built and driven as in the value-adoption harness (in-process replicas with the package's own handlers and marshaled RPC structs, FIFO delivery, no delivery to crashed replicas). Scenario: replica 1 holds a conflicting command so the owner's pre-accept replies are not equal; owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0) at ballot 0, enters the Accept phase and broadcasts Accept to replicas 1 and 2 (their AcceptReplies are left in flight, i.e. the owner is slow); replica 2 then recovers the same instance at its own ballot 7, so replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4 join ballot 7 and record bal 7, and replica 2 fails after broadcasting that Prepare; the owner then runs two ordinary startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) attempts (as its executor does after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD), and finally a third attempt after the target's own BeTheLeader handler is invoked on it, followed by completion of the quiescent exchange.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers; InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE, and only instance (0,0) is used.

The owner's AcceptReplies from replicas 1 and 2 are never delivered, modelling a slow owner whose recovery timers on the other replicas fire while the replies are in flight; the recovery of an instance whose owner is slow is a normal EPaxos event.
Replica 2's failure is modelled as: no further message is delivered to it, its queue is discarded and every replica's Alive flag for it is cleared.
Replica 1's conflicting command comes from a real startPhase1 whose auxiliary broadcast is discarded; only its local conflict state is used.
IsLeader is set through the target's own BeTheLeader handler, the same RPC the master invokes, and no production logic is modified.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path for the owner, injects the higher-ballot Prepare of replica 2 through handlePrepare at replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4, then calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at the owner three times, delivering every emitted Prepare to the peers' handlePrepare and every PrepareReply back to the owner, and recording the owner's tried ballot, the peers' stored ballots, the appended reply count and any follow-up message. Between attempts 2 and 3 it invokes replica 0's own BeTheLeader handler.
experiment.requirement: Recovery authority must be acquirable by the replica that runs the recovery: each recovery attempt must either produce a matching-ballot prepare quorum so that a sub-case is dispatched, or the next attempt at the same instance must use a ballot above the ballots the answering quorum reports, so that a stalled instance can still be recovered.
experiment.responsibility: The target's own ballot policy and nack handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 makeBallot, epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235 handlePrepareReply), not the environment or a caller: the peers answer honestly with the ballot they stored, and the repeated attempts are the executor's own retry path (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

comparisons.description: Without the designated-leader authority, a recovery attempt at an instance whose answering quorum reports a higher stored ballot still reaches SlowQuorumSize appended replies and dispatches a sub-case; violated when appended_replies stays 1 and no follow-up message is emitted.

The retry ballot exceeds the ballot the peers already stored, so the retry can act on the instance; violated when tried_ballot stays at 0 while stored_bal_before_attempt is 7 on both repeated attempts.
Control: after the target's own BeTheLeader handler runs, the attempt uses a ballot above the stored one and the sub-case dispatch happens; expected to hold.
Control outcome: with the authority granted, the owner's recovery completes the instance (status COMMITTED) and keeps the accepted command X; expected to hold.
